newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt mostly lower in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt mostly lower in late trade.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mostly lower in moderate afternoon trade but emerging market sources noted that the assets of the three major Latin American countries clearly outperformed U.S. Treasuries.

"Generally, our market has done okay. Spreads on Brazil and Argentina have tightened by about 10 basis points against U.S. Treasuries and Mexico (narrowed) by about five basis points," said one trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
On a price basis, Argentine FRBs were unchanged at 88-3/4 bid, Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/4 stronger at 75-5/8 and Mexican pars were were 3/8 softer at 74 bid.
Emerging market sources said, however, that a slew of U.S. economic data due out this week has created a bit of nervousness in the market.
"The ECI (employment cost index) will clearly be important for the U.S. Treasury market overall and indirectly for the Brady sector," said one market source.
Other U.S. data due out this week includes the consumer confidence report on Tuesday, Durable goods orders on Wednesday and the fourth quarter gross domestic product (GDP) on Friday.
In the broader sector of the market, Ecuadoran debt prices slipped amid growing concerns about the passage of the economic package and the convertability of the currency.
Ecuadoran pars were 1/2 lower at 45-1/2 bid.

"I don't think the fundatmental story is making people too comfortable right now," said another trader. However, he pointed out that Ecuador is still one of the cheapest Latin credits trading around 800 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Among the Eastern European assets, sources said yield spreads on Bulgarian paper widened by about 10 basis points over mounting concerns about the country's economic and political situation.

"At this point, I think there are are significant problems in putting a government together which is capable of implementing the necessary preconditions for the currency board. There is a lot of uncertainty," said an executive director at a European bank based in New York.

The source added that decisive macroeconomic management and political management "is absolutely vital and the longer it takes, the more dangerous it gets before the country really gets into a hyperinflation situation."
Meanwhile, Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans were 7/8 lower at 78 bid.
Sources attributed the drop in Russian loans to continued uncertainty over the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.

Earlier today, Yeltsin cancelled a trip to Europe becuase of health reasons. A Kremlin spokesman in Moscow said that doctors had advised Yeltsin, who is recovering from pneumonia, to refrain from air travel and to work at home.
